note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`.

personas.name: normal-adequate-study
personas.description: Fully normal 24-hour ABPM, adequate recording, complete report: every axis at its baseline — normal / none / routine, 100% complete.

state.clinicalHistory: Routine hypertension surveillance, no new symptoms
state.findingsNarrative: All averaged readings within normal ambulatory limits; normal dipping pattern.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: Consistent with prior study 12 months ago

expected.recommendedAction: No specific follow-up required; manage per usual care.

firedRules.description: No abnormal interpretation on an adequate recording; classified as normal.
No abnormal finding; abnormality severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: stage1-minor-raised-24h-average
personas.description: 24-hour average 132/81 crosses the 130/80 threshold, but the daytime average stays below 135/85 and no structured hypertension boolean is confirmed — abnormal, minor severity, stage-1 category.

state.clinicalHistory: Borderline clinic readings over the past 6 months
state.findingsNarrative: 24-hour average mildly raised; daytime average within normal limits.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Lifestyle advice; repeat ABPM in 6 months

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend lifestyle advice and follow-up monitoring per NICE NG136; consider treatment by cardiovascular risk.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal interpretations (raised average or confirmed/masked/nocturnal hypertension) are present; classified as abnormal.
Raised ambulatory average below the stage-2 threshold; severity graded minor.
Minor abnormality (stage 1, nocturnal, or white-coat); structured follow-up recommended.

personas.name: stage2-moderate-confirmed-hypertension
personas.description: Confirmed hypertension documented by the reporting clinician, daytime average 140/88 — below the 150/95 stage-2 numeric cutoff but the confirmed-hypertension boolean alone is sufficient to grade moderate/stage-2 severity.

state.clinicalHistory: Persistently raised clinic readings, known left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG
state.findingsNarrative: Sustained ambulatory hypertension consistent with clinic readings; non-dipping pattern.
state.comparisonWithPrevious: Progression from stage 1 six months ago
state.recommendedFollowUp: Initiate/intensify antihypertensive therapy; review in 4-6 weeks

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend antihypertensive treatment initiation or review per NICE NG136.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal interpretations (raised average or confirmed/masked/nocturnal hypertension) are present; classified as abnormal.
Stage 2 hypertension (ABPM daytime average >= 150/95) or confirmed / masked hypertension present; severity graded moderate.
Moderate abnormality present; follow-up recommended.

flags.description: Hypertension is confirmed on ambulatory averages and requires action.
flags.suggestedAction: Ensure the referrer is alerted and a treatment / management plan is documented per NICE NG136.

flags.description: Masked or nocturnal hypertension is present and carries elevated cardiovascular risk.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider referral to a hypertension specialist for further assessment.

personas.name: critical-severe-hypertension
personas.description: Daytime average 155/98 crosses the severe 150/95 threshold (ABPM-equivalent to clinic >= 180/120): auto-escalates classification to critical, severity to major, and follow-up to same-day critical-alert regardless of the other axes.

state.findingsNarrative: Severe sustained hypertension throughout the recording period with minimal nocturnal dip.
state.impression: Severe (grade 3) ambulatory hypertension — urgent review required.
state.clinicianNotes: Telephoned referrer directly at 14:20, results discussed and same-day clinic slot arranged.

expected.recommendedAction: Arrange same-day specialist review and communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now; document the conversation.

firedRules.description: A severe-hypertension result (ABPM average >= 150/95, equivalent to clinic >= 180/120) is present; classified as critical.
Severe hypertension present; abnormality severity graded major.
Severe hypertension auto-escalates follow-up urgency to critical-alert regardless of the other axes (NICE NG136 same-day specialist review).

flags.description: A severe-hypertension result (ABPM average >= 150/95, equivalent to clinic >= 180/120) is present.
flags.suggestedAction: Arrange same-day specialist review and communicate the critical result to the referrer immediately; document the communication.

flags.description: Masked or nocturnal hypertension is present and carries elevated cardiovascular risk.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider referral to a hypertension specialist for further assessment.

personas.name: masked-hypertension
personas.description: Masked hypertension confirmed by the clinician while every averaged measurement stays below its own threshold (normal clinic readings, raised ambulatory pattern is the whole point of masked hypertension) — the structured boolean alone grades moderate/stage-2.

state.clinicalHistory: Normal clinic readings but asymptomatic left ventricular hypertrophy noted incidentally
state.findingsNarrative: Ambulatory pattern discordant with clinic readings — masked hypertension.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Initiate antihypertensive therapy; repeat ABPM to confirm response

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend antihypertensive treatment initiation or review per NICE NG136.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal interpretations (raised average or confirmed/masked/nocturnal hypertension) are present; classified as abnormal.
Stage 2 hypertension (ABPM daytime average >= 150/95) or confirmed / masked hypertension present; severity graded moderate.
Moderate abnormality present; follow-up recommended.

flags.description: Masked or nocturnal hypertension is present and carries elevated cardiovascular risk.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider referral to a hypertension specialist for further assessment.

personas.name: isolated-nocturnal-hypertension-non-dipper
personas.description: Nighttime average 122/72 crosses the 120/70 nocturnal threshold with a non-dipping pattern (2% dip), while daytime and 24-hour averages stay normal — isolated nocturnal hypertension, minor severity.

state.clinicalHistory: Known type 2 diabetes, screening for non-dipping pattern
state.findingsNarrative: Isolated nocturnal hypertension with a non-dipping pattern; daytime readings normal.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Review medication timing (consider evening dosing); cardiovascular risk assessment

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend lifestyle advice and follow-up monitoring per NICE NG136; consider treatment by cardiovascular risk.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal interpretations (raised average or confirmed/masked/nocturnal hypertension) are present; classified as abnormal.
Isolated nocturnal hypertension present; severity graded minor.

flags.suggestedAction: Consider referral to a hypertension specialist for further assessment.

personas.name: white-coat-effect
personas.description: Raised clinic blood pressure but every ambulatory average is within normal limits — the white-coat-effect boolean is what makes this abnormal (not a normal study) rather than the numbers themselves.

state.clinicalHistory: Clinic BP consistently 155/95, requested to rule out white-coat effect before starting treatment
state.findingsNarrative: All ambulatory averages normal despite persistently raised clinic readings — white-coat effect.
state.impression: White-coat effect; true ambulatory blood pressure is normal.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No pharmacological treatment indicated; continue annual monitoring

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend lifestyle advice and follow-up monitoring per NICE NG136; consider treatment by cardiovascular risk.

firedRules.description: White-coat effect present (raised clinic BP but normal ambulatory averages); classified as abnormal (not a normal study).
White-coat effect present; severity graded minor.
Minor abnormality (stage 1, nocturnal, or white-coat); structured follow-up recommended.

flags.description: A white-coat effect is documented (raised clinic BP but normal ambulatory averages).
flags.suggestedAction: Manage per the relevant white-coat-hypertension pathway and document.

personas.name: inconclusive-inadequate-recording
personas.description: Only 45% of readings were valid — below the 70% adequacy threshold — and no impression was recorded: the study is inconclusive rather than assumed normal or abnormal.

state.clinicalHistory: Device removed early by patient due to discomfort
state.findingsNarrative: Insufficient valid readings to interpret reliably.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Repeat ABPM with reinforced patient instructions

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend repeat ambulatory or home monitoring to obtain an adequate study.

firedRules.description: Recording was inadequate (< 70% valid readings) and no impression was recorded; classified as inconclusive.
Inconclusive study; abnormality severity not established.
Mandatory report section missing: averaged blood-pressure measurements.
Mandatory report section missing: nocturnal dipping.
Mandatory report section missing: impression.
Inconclusive or inadequate recording; repeat monitoring recommended.

flags.description: Recording adequacy is below the 70% valid-readings threshold; diagnostic confidence may be reduced.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider repeating the monitoring period to obtain an adequate study.

flags.description: No impression / conclusion has been recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Add an impression that answers the clinical question.

flags.description: No daytime or 24-hour average blood pressure was recorded.
flags.suggestedAction: Record the averaged blood-pressure measurements for interpretation.
